annotations.text:
RACK FIRST — one direction, done properly.

The rack, its faceplates, real ports from the engine's catalogue, and cables that sag between them are the product. Everything else hangs off that.

What I took from Homelable: the slack-loop cable (bows right and down, more on longer runs), real RJ45/SFP jack shapes at a fixed size, patch-facing gear always shows ports and everything else reveals on hover, one cable per port, copper-or-fibre decided by the port you start from.

What I took from elsewhere: Patchdocs lights the WHOLE physical path on one hover — that is the answer to your crossing complaint. Device42 keeps power and data cabling on separate toggles. Meraki/Mist put L2/L3 facts on the port, so you never leave the rack to read them.

What I dropped: the building view (not necessary — you said so), the black triangle cursors (presence is now a dashed ring on the device someone is editing plus a name chip on the rail; a held port gets a dashed ring too), and the six-tab bar.

Answered 2026-09-11:
✓ Colour: by cable type by default (copper blue, OM4 aqua, OS2 yellow, power black), overridable per lead. The phantom effect — off-path cables at 28%, on-path haloed — is unchanged.
✓ Ports: RJ45, SFP+ (bail), LC (two ferrules) and C14 (power) are now four distinct glyphs.
✓ PSUs: dual/single PSU inlets notated on the left rail at rack scale; the rear face shows them in place when zoomed, with the PDU outlet that feeds each. A single-fed device is marked.
✓ Rear view: proposed as front-over-rear stacked at faceplate zoom, a flip at rack scale.

Still open:
• Portal styling — dashed trays, or a cable that visibly runs off the edge?
• Presence without cursors — enough?
Kept for the record. You rejected all eight on 2026-09-11 — the rack was not the centrepiece in any of them, and the building view hid crossings. Nothing here is in play.
